review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] attributes, no simp-set definitions and no custom simp lemmas. Every simp use is a one-off `simp` or `simp only` call inside a proof. I checked Mathlib's `PowerSeries.coeff_X_pow`. It is already @[simp], so the file relies on existing simp coverage. `coeff_mul_X_pow'` is not simp. It is a conditional rewrite that the file applies explicitly with `rw`, which suits it. The three theorems (`exists_X_sub_C_pow_eq`, `coeff_pred_eq`, `exists_coeff_low_eq`) are existential statements about specific expressions. They are not normal-form rewrite rules, so tagging them simp would be unjustified. I found no rewrite in a bad direction, no competing rules, no unwanted expansion and no credible rewrite cycle. The duplicated `h1`–`h4` blocks in two proofs are a proof-reuse matter, not a simp-interface defect under this rubric. I could not run Lean, so I made no claim about simp behaviour.
